doc.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022

title: Role of jazz in society today
summary: Monk asks what role jazz has now; Aebersold thinks little, though schools embrace it.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yeah it’s a shame that jazz has almost zero presence on television and cable. I mean you have to go out of your way to find it. But I’ve been trying to formulate a question, I’m not successful yet, but it seems like jazz has had different roles and exposure in American society and it’s changed a lot. I haven’t figured out what the role of jazz is today, in today’s world.
I don’t think it has much role.

But it’s ironic that I just got the last DownBeat issue and it’s the sort of where to go to school issue. And it’s hundreds, literally hundreds of schools, and they’re just the ones that decided to put an ad in the DownBeat. So if it doesn’t have much of a role, why is it that it’s been so elevated and embraced by academia?
